course_summary:
ISEN 616 | Design and Analysis of Industrial Experiments | Spring 2026
Instructor: Rui Tuo | ruituo@tamu.edu
Meets: MWF 08:00AM-08:50AM | ZACH 211
Grading: Homework [10%], Exam 1 [20%], Exam 2 [20%], Final Exam [30%], Group Project [20%] — A: 90%-100%, B: 80%-89.9%, C: 70%-79.9%, D: 60%-69.9%, F: less than 60%
Topics: Taguchi methods, response surface methodologies, Orthogonal arrays, maximum resolution, minimum aberration, robust parameter design for product and process improvement, fractional factorial experiments at three levels, Fractional factorial experiments at two levels, full and fractional two-level factorial experiments, factorial experiments at two levels, 'one-factor-at-a-time' plans, Latin and other squares, treatment comparison procedures, one-factor experiments with and without restrictions on randomization, blocking in factorial designs, choice of optimal blocking schemes, analysis of location and dispersion, Variation reduction, off-line experimentation techniques, industrial experimental design, statistical data analysis, model building, engineering formulations, design tools, data-collecting, experiment planning capability, fundamental principles of design, analytical procedures, concepts, formulations, applications, fundamental theory
Tools: R statistical software package, Canvas
Prerequisites: STAT 212 or STAT 601
